Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Nearly every outlet in this group is dominated by the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO amid a scandal involving alleged affairs and Chinese espionage concerns, with coverage spanning the succession hunt, Washington's political fallout, and market jitters. Alongside that, Anthropic's imminent IPO, a prolonged Microsoft outage, and oil-market tension tied to Iran are also drawing heavy attention.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid affair and spy scandal
stories.summary: Jensen Huang's three-decade run at Nvidia ended abruptly after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is linked to Chinese intelligence; Axios reported Nvidia shares fell as much as 13% on the news and the company has lost roughly $1.4 trillion in market value in two weeks. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO and Harvey Jones became the company's first-ever board chair.

stories.headline: The hunt for Nvidia's next permanent CEO
stories.summary: With no clear succession plan in place, Fortune reports speculation ranges from internal contenders like Nvidia veteran Ian Buck to external names including Apple's Tim Cook (who Trump publicly backed), Google Cloud's Tom Kurian, AMD's Lisa Su, and even members of Huang's own family. Axios and the BBC separately profiled interim CEO Colette Kress and other possible successors as the board, led by new chair Harvey Jones, begins its search.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO becomes a test for the AI trade amid Nvidia turmoil
stories.summary: Anthropic is targeting a valuation of roughly $1.33 trillion or more as it prepares to begin trading, with CEO Dario Amodei telling Jamie Dimon he hopes the offering will "underpromise and overdeliver." Fortune and Bloomberg noted the IPO, pricing shares between $70-$78, is seen as a crucial confidence test for the AI sector just as Nvidia's leadership crisis rattles investors.

stories.headline: Bessent blames Commerce Department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly faulted the Commerce Department for not sanctioning Singapore-based Megaspeed, the firm tied to Jensen Huang's alleged spy scandal, and said Nvidia employees should be held accountable if they sidestepped export law. The Washington Post and FT reported the rare public clash risks exposing deeper tensions between Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick within the Trump administration, while Puck detailed a reported Situation Room confrontation between the two.

stories.headline: Microsoft battles a second day of global outages
stories.summary: Microsoft described "encouraging" progress on efforts to resolve a second day of disruptions to Outlook, Teams and other services, as the BBC detailed ongoing concerns over lost emails and how long the fix would take.

stories.headline: Iran drone strike on Bahrain raises Gulf tensions, rattles oil markets
stories.summary: The U.S. said it intercepted an Iranian drone strike on Bahrain, the first known attack on the Gulf country in two months, feeding into oil-price volatility after Trump questioned the need for a new Iran deal. Bloomberg's oil market coverage likewise noted crude fluctuating as traders weighed conflicting signals on US-Iran peace talks.

stories.headline: US home sales hit worst slump since the Great Recession's aftermath
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports that home sales are slumping badly as elevated mortgage rates push up the typical monthly payment facing U.S. homebuyers, marking the weakest stretch for the housing market in years.

stories.headline: Chicago's third CFO exit this year fuels credit rating worries
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Chicago has lost its third chief financial officer this year, raising concerns about the city's credit ratings as it tries to close an $882 million budget deficit.

Business.gaps: Business Insider had no identifiable recent feed items or search results surfaced in this run.

US politics.overview: Coverage across US politics outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid a Chinese espionage scandal, which has triggered infighting among Trump's cabinet, and by Sen. Chris Van Hollen's surprise challenge to Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader. Outlets are also digging into the midterm aftermath, including a Supreme Court asylum case, a failed Hegseth impeachment push, and analysis of why Democrats swept the South.

stories.headline: Van Hollen challenges Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader, arguing Democrats need new leadership, while Schumer quickly rallied several colleagues' public endorsements and insists he has the votes to win the Dec. 1 election.

stories.headline: Trump's economic advisers clash over Nvidia chip export failures
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department for failing to restrict Nvidia chip sales to the company at the center of former CEO Jensen Huang's spy scandal, deepening a cabinet rift; Courthouse News reports Bessent's criticism has put Lutnick under increasing scrutiny given his close ties to Huang.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear Trump's asylum restrictions case
stories.summary: The administration asked the Supreme Court to greenlight Trump's unilateral authority to shut down asylum applications at the southern border, after lower courts ruled the Inauguration Day restrictions illegal.

stories.headline: Hegseth impeachment effort collapses in the House
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth narrowly avoided becoming only the third cabinet secretary ever impeached after 11 absent Democrats failed to reach the House floor in time to vote.

stories.headline: Black voter turnout surge powered Democrats' sweep across the South
stories.summary: NPR's analysis of six Deep South states found the leftward swing in the midterms was driven by high Black voter turnout combined with a sharp decline in Republican-leaning turnout; Stateline similarly reports voting advocates say the result reflects more than a generic "blue wave."

stories.headline: Pence calls GOP midterm losses 'a reckoning' over Iran, tariffs and corruption
stories.summary: Former Vice President Mike Pence argued in an exclusive interview that Republicans' embrace of Trump's populist agenda, including the Iran war and tariffs, produced a political reckoning rather than a routine midterm setback.

stories.headline: Democrats reach a fragile détente in their internal ideological war
stories.summary: A new POLITICO poll finds moderates and progressives feeling more unified after the midterms, though cracks remain over how to deliver for voters heading into 2028.

stories.headline: Congress edges toward a shutdown fight over Iran war funding
stories.summary: Punchbowl News reports Congress is almost certain to miss a full-year funding deal by the Dec. 11 deadline, with Democrats under pressure to use government funding leverage to cut off money for the Iran war while Trump takes a hard line.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS's search results returned mostly older archived content rather than current 24-48 hour coverage, so no fresh NOTUS story could be confidently included. SCOTUSblog, The Dispatch and National Review newsletter-style items were captured mainly via their feed headlines rather than full web search detail.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across nearly every outlet is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid an espionage-tinged affair scandal, and by Microsoft's crippling multi-day global cloud outage. Secondary threads include Anthropic's blockbuster IPO (set to be the largest in history), OpenAI's push into agentic commerce with ChatGPT Wallet, and mounting evidence that Chinese AI labs are using export-banned Nvidia chips.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's ouster from Nvidia triggers industry-wide reckoning
stories.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid a scandal involving an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Wall Street fearing it could slow Nvidia's AI dealmaking given the company's $48B stake in 229 startups and $500B lending consortium now in flux.

stories.headline: Microsoft's global cloud outage stretches into a second day
stories.summary: Microsoft says a bad update, not a cyberattack, caused Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other 365 services to fail worldwide for roughly 24 hours, disrupting governments, hospitals, schools and businesses before beginning to recover.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO is six times oversubscribed, on track to be the largest ever
stories.summary: Anthropic is heading toward the biggest public offering in history, with investor demand for its IPO shares exceeding supply by a factor of six as the company targets a valuation above $1.33 trillion.

stories.headline: Evidence mounts that China's top AI models run on banned Nvidia chips
stories.summary: New research indicates China's most advanced AI models were trained on Nvidia chips subject to US export bans, adding to a parallel finding from a former OpenAI researcher claiming to have found Nvidia Blackwell GPU fingerprints inside six Chinese AI models.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI agent shopping
stories.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf in a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers, marking OpenAI's second attempt at agentic commerce after scrapping its earlier Instant Checkout feature.

stories.headline: Arm's Rene Haas approached in search for Nvidia's next CEO
stories.summary: The head of SoftBank-owned chip designer Arm has been contacted as part of Nvidia's search for a permanent chief executive following Jensen Huang's resignation over affairs.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster Flash successor
stories.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, which the company says completes tasks 2.5 times as fast as Gemini 3.8 Flash and scored ahead of its predecessor on independent benchmarking by Artificial Analysis.

stories.headline: Uber confirms driver's license data stolen in breach tied to AI vendor Fireworks
stories.summary: Uber said thousands of drivers' license records stored by AI cloud company Fireworks AI were stolen in a security incident, with VentureBeat separately reporting the same Fireworks breach also exposed Notion AI chat transcripts.

Tech & AI.gaps: Google DeepMind had no new company announcements found in this window. IEEE Spectrum's recent posts were not timely news items relevant to this cycle. The Verge, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, and The Guardian were assessed only via the provided feed items and/or limited search snippets, not full-site browsing.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, where UN chief António Guterres delivered a blistering closing message on fossil fuels even as new deals (China-Turkey renewables, UK-Japan offshore wind) were struck on the sidelines. U.S.-focused outlets are parsing how last week's Democratic midterm sweep will reshape energy and climate politics, while oil markets stayed volatile on conflicting signals about U.S.-Iran diplomacy, and utility-sector trade press tracked grid, permitting and data-center fights across the U.S.

stories.headline: UN chief's closing climate message: Fossil fuels are 'killing our planet'
stories.summary: In what is likely his final speech before COP31 as UN Secretary-General, Guterres said the world remains on a path to "mutually assured destruction" and accused fossil fuel interests of profiting while destroying the planet.

stories.headline: Midterm sweep set to reshape US energy and climate politics
stories.summary: Heatmap argues that Democrats' election wins came by moderating climate rhetoric toward affordability and "all of the above" energy messaging, while Latitude Media separately reports the party's new state-level majorities are now strategizing how to turn ratepayer-focused wins into policy.

stories.headline: Oil prices swing on mixed signals over US-Iran diplomacy
stories.summary: Oil prices rebounded and closed higher after President Trump said the U.S. doesn't need a deal with Iran, reinjecting risk premium into the market after earlier losses.

stories.headline: Exxon Mobil sues the EU over its carbon capture rules
stories.summary: Exxon filed a confidential legal challenge to EU carbon capture regulations, in what the Financial Times called the latest attempt by the company to "row back Brussels' flagship green regulations," according to Heatmap.

stories.headline: California climate disclosure laws face split appeals court ruling
stories.summary: The Ninth Circuit allowed SB 253's Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions reporting requirements to proceed while halting enforcement of Scope 3 reporting and the related SB 261 climate-risk disclosure law.

stories.headline: U.S. oil embargo pushes Cuba to run on American fuel shipments
stories.summary: Growing American fuel shipments are keeping Cuba's energy system afloat after Trump's oil embargo pushed the island toward a humanitarian crisis, WSJ reports.

stories.headline: Renewables and storage to meet most new power demand as coal declines: EIA
stories.summary: The EIA projects the power sector could add more than 26 GW of battery storage next year, with renewables supplying nearly a quarter of generation as coal use keeps falling and overall demand rises.

Energy.gaps: E&E News appears to have stopped publishing standalone content (its site now redirects to POLITICO Pro), so no current 24-48h coverage could be verified beyond older archived headlines. Argus Media could not be found via search and had no feed items, so its current coverage is unknown. Reuters, FT, NYT and The Economist block search and had no feed items provided, so their current energy/climate coverage could not be assessed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Taiwanese, Hong Kong and international outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid a China-espionage scandal, just as Washington and Beijing position for the APEC summit in Shenzhen and further Trump-Xi engagement. Alongside the Huang story, outlets are tracking renewed Chinese military pressure on Taiwan, trade and export data showing China's AI-driven export boom, and a wave of corporate and EV-sector news.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid China spy scandal
stories.summary: Nvidia's board announced that Huang has resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, after allegations emerged that he had an intimate relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, plunging the company at the center of the US-China AI rivalry into crisis just before a planned Trump-Xi meeting at the APEC summit.

stories.headline: Taiwan says China's unannounced drills were 'silent intimidation'
stories.summary: Taiwanese officials described a large, unannounced Chinese military exercise across the western Pacific and around Taiwan earlier this month as a campaign of "silent intimidation," with more than 100 vessels massed and simulated attacks on other militaries and cities, including Taiwan's.

stories.headline: US-China Board of Trade holds first meeting ahead of Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: The United States and China held the inaugural meeting of their bilateral Board of Trade, a new framework agreed earlier this year, just days before Trump is set to meet Xi again.

stories.headline: China's export boom accelerates on AI-related trade
stories.summary: Customs figures show dollar-denominated exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier while imports accelerated to 41.6%, with analysts pointing to continued strength in AI-related exports and improving demand for other industrial goods as the drivers behind the resilience.

stories.headline: Huawei set to post record revenue, but profitability takes a hit
stories.summary: Huawei Technologies is on track to surpass its record annual revenue this year, a comeback driven by heavy investment in AI chips and its homegrown operating system, though the push has come at a cost to its bottom line.

stories.headline: Chinese EV makers roll out new models and expand battery-swap networks
stories.summary: CATL unveiled plans to build 6,000 passenger-car battery swap stations by 2027 covering nearly 300 Chinese cities, as rivals including BYD's Denza, Nissan, Huawei-backed Aito, Xpeng and Voyah simultaneously launched or previewed new SUVs and expanded overseas retail footprints.

stories.headline: A franchise revolution is reshaping Chinese retail
stories.summary: A wave of franchising is spreading buzzy Chinese retail brands into every corner of the country and increasingly abroad, according to the magazine's latest business coverage.

stories.headline: Trump casts doubt on Jimmy Lai's release, citing Chinese 'hatred'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said China harbours intense animosity toward jailed Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai, suggesting Beijing is unlikely to release the pro-democracy figure.

China.gaps: No recent standalone coverage could be found via search for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Yicai Global, ChinaTalk, China Daily or CGTN; Xinhua appeared only as a secondary source quoted inside other outlets' reporting rather than through its own current articles.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by escalating US-Iran tensions in the Gulf, including a disputed radar strike and drone interception near Bahrain and a tanker mine blast in the Strait of Hormuz, alongside fallout from Trump's remark that Saudi Arabia is 'disintegrating.' Regional diplomacy (a new Turkey-Qatar defence pact, Turkey's expanding role in Lebanon), Gaza's worsening humanitarian crisis, and ripple effects from the Nvidia leadership scandal are also prominent themes.

stories.headline: Trump says Saudi Arabia is 'disintegrating'
stories.summary: Trump said in an interview that Saudi Arabia is 'disintegrating' and that Gulf states have asked him not to resume war with Iran because they are too vulnerable to further fallout, remarks likely to anger Riyadh.

stories.headline: Turkey, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement, pledge unified stance against attack
stories.summary: Turkey and Qatar signed a new mutual defence pact aimed at strengthening collective security and pledged a unified response to any external armed attack on either country.

stories.headline: US shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones launched towards Bahrain
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain and reported a gas tanker hit a mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington denied the radar strike and said it intercepted two Iranian drones instead.

stories.headline: Gaza baby dies from exposure to cold as WHO warns of rising infection rates
stories.summary: A baby in Gaza died from cold exposure as the WHO warned of rising infection rates in the territory, highlighting the deepening humanitarian toll as a US-brokered peace plan remains stalled.

stories.headline: How will the US deal with Nvidia scandal?
stories.summary: Nvidia's CEO resigned amid a widening scandal and is expected to testify before Congress, a story being watched closely in the Gulf given the region's heavy AI-chip investments tied to the company.

stories.headline: UAE companies turn to share buybacks following sell-offs
stories.summary: AGBI reports UAE-listed firms are increasingly repurchasing their own shares after recent market sell-offs, while separately noting Saudi oil production has held steady despite intensifying Houthi attacks on energy infrastructure.

stories.headline: IMF says more progress needed on Lebanon's banking sector reform
stories.summary: The IMF said Lebanon has not yet made sufficient headway reforming its banking sector, a key condition for unlocking broader international financial support as the country struggles with economic crisis.

stories.headline: Why is Erdogan's son meeting Lebanon's top leaders?
stories.summary: Bilal Erdogan has been meeting senior Lebanese political figures as Ankara seeks a larger diplomatic role in Lebanon, even as the Lebanese army separately raided an arms depot in Beirut's southern suburbs.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No current (last 24-48h) stories could be found for Arab News, Arabian Business (beyond a static awards-event listing), Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Ynetnews, Haaretz, or Iran International.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across African outlets this week centers on a global Microsoft cloud outage that exposed African banks' dependence on US tech, security and humanitarian fallout from Guinea's mass expulsion of Burkinabe gold miners and an Ebola scare at a major DRC mine, and continuing fallout from US trade/visa policy (AGOA exclusion, Trump's DRC ambassador pick) alongside South Africa's post-election political realignment.

stories.headline: Microsoft's global outage exposes African banks' reliance on Big Tech
stories.summary: A roughly 18-hour Microsoft outage disrupted South African firms and institutions including Eskom, Absa and FlySafair, while Kenyan banks and insurers lost email access for over 15 hours and had to fall back on WhatsApp and phone lines, underlining the continent's dependence on a single US cloud provider.

stories.headline: Barrick furloughs staff at Congo's Kibali gold mine over Ebola precaution
stories.summary: Barrick Mining is furloughing some employees and subcontractors at its Kibali gold mine in the DRC after officials reported two Ebola deaths in a nearby community, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters.

stories.headline: Guinea's expulsion of Burkinabe gold miners triggers diplomatic and humanitarian fallout
stories.summary: Since November 6, more than 37,000 Burkinabe nationals, including some 8,000 children, have been returning home after being expelled from Guinea, prompting Burkinabe authorities to pledge support for the returnees.

stories.headline: Trump names little-known pastor as US ambassador to DRC
stories.summary: John Mark Burns, a South Carolina preacher with no diplomatic experience, has been tapped to fill a DRC ambassadorial post left vacant for nearly a year as Washington tightens its focus on Congo's cobalt resources.

stories.headline: South Africa's ANC grapples with the fallout of its municipal election slump
stories.summary: Africa Confidential reports that South Africa's political order is fragmenting after the ANC's municipal retreat, with established political brokers rather than young activists driving the realignment inside Ramaphosa's coalition.

stories.headline: Ramaphosa pushes AI investment trip to US despite visa sanctions and AGOA exclusion
stories.summary: Despite Washington's visa restrictions and diplomatic hostility, South Africa's president is leading a high-powered delegation to California seeking tech investment, a trip that comes as African Business separately details the economic costs to South Africa and Rwanda from their exclusion from AGOA.

stories.headline: Nigerian banks hit by costly wave of cyberattacks in October
stories.summary: A wave of cyberattacks in early October led to fraud losses at several Nigerian banks and financial institutions, potentially costing billions of naira in customer funds, according to multiple sources cited by TechCabal.

stories.headline: Foreign investors tighten grip on Kenya's $23bn retail sector
stories.summary: Following Quickmart's oversubscribed IPO, US and UK investors now control roughly 60% of Kenya's supermarket sector alongside Naivas and Carrefour, even as low-cost Chinese retailers mount a fresh competitive challenge.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no verifiable recent (last 48h) coverage available beyond older archived issues, so it is not represented in this report. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ could not be searched directly and no relevant feed items were provided for them.

Media.overview: Media coverage over the past 24-48 hours centers heavily on turmoil at CBS News (Face the Nation leadership exits, credibility questions from Scott Pelley) and CNN (contract uncertainty for star anchors), alongside the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's sudden departure being refracted through a media/political lens. Trade outlets are also tracking AI's growing footprint in newsrooms and Hollywood (from local-news bots to editors and The Ringer dropping ChatGPT), a tragic on-set death at Netflix's 'Dept. Q,' and policy fights over tech platforms paying for news in Indonesia.

stories.headline: Face the changes: Two top leaders are leaving CBS News' 'Face the Nation'
stories.summary: Mary Hager, senior executive producer of 'Face the Nation,' is leaving CBS News after 35 years in a leadership shakeup that Status first reported.

stories.headline: Scott Pelley says CBS has lost its credibility. A post-midterms about-face wouldn't help.
stories.summary: Amid a Democratic midterm 'tsunami,' questions are swirling over whether CBS leadership that tried to appease President Trump will now reverse course, with veteran anchor Scott Pelley warning the network has lost credibility.

stories.headline: CNN's Contract Cliff
stories.summary: Status reports that with contracts approaching expiration under Skydance, the futures of CNN anchors Brianna Keilar and Clarissa Ward are uncertain, while network boss Mark Thompson also remains without a deal; separately, CNN's New York bureau is facing an abrupt, major exit.

stories.headline: Right- and Left-Leaning Media Both Put Trump at the Center of Nvidia Scandal, but For Different Reasons
stories.summary: Mediaite notes that both right- and left-leaning outlets are framing President Trump as central to the unfolding scandal around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure, a story Adweek's Carl Quintanilla interview separately called a potential major corporate scandal.

stories.headline: Indonesia's new copyright bill would force Google and Meta to pay to aggregate news
stories.summary: Meta, TikTok, and Google testified before Indonesia's parliament this week in opposition to a proposed copyright law that would require digital platforms to pay news publishers for aggregating their content.

stories.headline: Netflix's 'Dept. Q' Crew Member Dies on Set in Edinburgh
stories.summary: Police are investigating the death of a crew member on the Netflix series' Edinburgh set, the second person to die during a production at FirstStage Studios, with producer Left Bank Pictures saying it is "deeply shocked and saddened."

stories.headline: London Police Investigating David Walliams Over Sexual Misconduct Allegations
stories.summary: London police have opened an investigation into the BAFTA-winning children's author following a bombshell Guardian and ITV investigation into misconduct allegations published this week.

stories.headline: Bill Simmons Ends The Ringer's ChatGPT Partnership After Fan Backlash
stories.summary: Spotify-owned The Ringer has scrapped its ChatGPT sponsorship experiment with AI-generated content after backlash from fans and even one of its own hosts.

stories.headline: With event costs up and funding down, journalism organizations cancel conferences and cut staff
stories.summary: Journalism conferences that rebounded after the pandemic are now being canceled or scaled back as organizations face rising costs and shrinking funding.

Media.gaps: Puck's homepage showed only evergreen newsletter descriptions rather than a specific story from the last 24-48 hours, so no distinct Puck item could be confirmed as current; NYT, WSJ, FT, and The Guardian block search and had no relevant media-industry feed items provided beyond a Cravath insider-trading item (WSJ) and a Hong Kong dissident podcast (Guardian), neither central to media-industry coverage.
